Title of the second 2026-09-17 release note. 'Integrated Strategies' is an in-game mode name and is never translated. A grade is this site's own letter rating of a player.
Label of the third 2026-09-17 release note's call to action, which opens the settings page where the switch lives.

entries.source_text: Appearance setting: show Latin names for CN-only operators. Applies to the operator list, operator pages, the planner and the search palette.
entries.description: Bullet in the third 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'New'. 'CN' is the Chinese game server's short name and stays as-is.

entries.source_text: The search palette now includes CN-only operators and matches their Latin name as strongly as any other name.
entries.description: Bullet in the third 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'Improved'. 'CN' is the Chinese game server's short name and stays as-is.

entries.source_text: Operators that have not reached the global server yet now show under the Latin-script name the game gives them, so 予愿安洁莉娜 reads as Angelina the Mellow Wish. It is an appearance setting, on by default, and search finds these operators by either name.
entries.description: Lead paragraph of the third 2026-09-17 release note, rendered as Markdown. The Chinese example and its Latin name are game data and stay as-is. 'Global server' is the English-language game server.
Title of the third 2026-09-17 release note. 'CN' is the Chinese game server's short name and stays as-is.
Label of the 2026-09-17 release note's call to action, which opens the release planner on its Pulls tab.

entries.source_text: Added a pull planner: budget one pool of rolls across upcoming banners and see which goals you can actually afford.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'New'. 'Rolls' and 'banners' are gacha terms.

entries.source_text: Pull odds are computed exactly, and cover every guarantee the game ships: soft and hard pity, rate-up guarantees, and the Limited spark.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'New'. 'Soft pity' is the rising-rate window, 'hard pity' the forced result, and 'spark' the exchange after a set number of rolls on a Limited banner. Keep the game's own terms.

entries.source_text: Rosters can be sorted by investment, scoring each operator against its own ceiling rather than against the roster.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'New'. 'Investment' means how far an operator has been levelled and upgraded.

entries.source_text: Signing in now asks whether to keep your game credentials with a "Keep me synced" choice, and declining deletes anything an earlier sign-in stored.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'New'. 'Keep me synced' is the control's own label and should be translated as a label.

entries.source_text: Settings now has a single Account section in place of separate Profile and Account & data panels.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'Improved'. 'Account', 'Profile' and 'Account & data' are settings panel names.

entries.source_text: Planner events read as their in-game names instead of raw tags, a banner matched only by date says so, and the calendar keeps its month header and legend in view while you scroll.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'Improved'.

entries.source_text: First sign-in no longer fails with "Failed to fetch user data", and signing in on mobile no longer signs you straight back out.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The quoted string is an error message the user saw in English; keep it recognisable.

entries.source_text: The roster's view mode and your chosen profile tab stay where you left them.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'View mode' is the roster's icons-or-list toggle.

entries.source_text: Removed the leaderboard's Skins sort, which ranked every player at 0.0%.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-17 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'Skins' are operator outfits.

entries.source_text: The planner's Pulls tab is live. It holds one ledger of your rolls across every upcoming banner, prices each goal against the pity you will actually be carrying when that banner lands, and shows what committing early to one banner costs you at the next. Login, roster and settings fixes from Discord feedback ship alongside it.
entries.description: Lead paragraph of the 2026-09-17 release note, rendered as Markdown. 'Pity' is the game's guarantee counter that improves the odds as rolls go without a top-rarity result; 'banner' is a time-limited gacha pool.
Title of the 2026-09-17 release note. 'Pull' is the community's word for a single gacha roll.
Label of the 2026-09-18 release note's call to action, which opens the release planner on its Pulls tab.

entries.source_text: The roster fits more operators per row at every width, and three per row on any phone rather than two on some and three on others.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Improved'. 'Roster' is a player's collection of operators.

entries.source_text: When a message's English is edited, its translation now shows the old and new wording word by word, instead of only being marked out of date.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Improved'. It describes the translation editor in the admin panel, which volunteer translators use.

entries.source_text: The translation editor explains a message's placeholders: which plural forms your language needs, which numbers each one covers, and the English wording for each.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Improved'. A 'placeholder' is a slot in a message that is filled with a value; a 'plural form' is one of the wordings a language selects between by number, such as one/few/many/other in Russian.

entries.source_text: Korean, Japanese and Chinese fell back to a mismatched typeface in small headings, and carried letter-spacing meant for the Latin alphabet that pushed the characters apart.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'Letter-spacing' is the extra space set between characters.

entries.source_text: The appearance switch's labels no longer break mid-word in a language whose word for 'Dark' is wider than the button.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The 'appearance switch' is the light/dark/auto control in the site header.

entries.source_text: The leaderboard's Top movers heading no longer runs into the column label beside it when it is translated into something longer.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'Top movers' is the card listing the players whose rank changed most.

entries.source_text: Orundum, Originite Prime, permits and certificates carry their own icons in the pull planner, and its smallest labels have been enlarged.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Improved'. Orundum, Originite Prime, Headhunting Permits and certificates are in-game currencies and keep the game's names.

entries.source_text: The pull planner's goals say what they measure: a specific rate-up, any rate-up, six copies of one. On a banner with more than two rate-ups the old wording claimed something the estimate never covered.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Improved'. A 'rate-up' is an operator with raised odds on a banner; a banner is a time-limited gacha pool.

entries.source_text: The Spark and Guarantee buttons ask for what you actually have to spend, with the banner's own free pulls already subtracted.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Improved'. A 'spark' is the pity exchange that trades a fixed number of pulls for an operator outright.

entries.source_text: Margins, page headings and the wording for players are consistent across the site; the leaderboard, search and profiles all say 'players' now.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Improved'. The site previously alternated between 'Doctors', the game's own word for the player, and 'Players'.

entries.source_text: Promotion ranks, potential ranks and mastery badges were nearly invisible on the light theme. They are legible again, and larger on phones.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. Promotion, potential and mastery are in-game operator upgrade systems.

entries.source_text: Stepping an operator's potential in the pull planner no longer stalls for about a second before the numbers move.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'Potential' is the in-game upgrade earned from duplicate copies of an operator.

entries.source_text: A banner's Clear button now clears the operators picked on it as well as the pulls, and a banner with no art of its own no longer borrows an unrelated event's picture or hides half its rate-up operators.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. A 'rate-up' is an operator with raised odds on a banner.

entries.source_text: Profile, settings and tier-list pages no longer scroll sideways by a few pixels on a phone.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-18 release note, filed under 'Fixed'.

entries.source_text: The roster fits more operators per row at every width, and its promotion, potential and mastery badges are legible on the light theme again. The pull planner's goals say what they measure, its currencies carry the game's own icons, and setting a potential no longer stalls before the numbers move. Margins and page headings are now shared across the site. Korean, Japanese and Chinese render in a matching typeface throughout, labels that used to break mid-word hold together, and the translation editor now explains a message's plural forms and shows what changed when its English moves.
entries.description: Lead paragraph of the 2026-09-18 release note, rendered as Markdown. 'Roster' is a player's collection of operators; promotion, potential and mastery are in-game upgrade systems; a 'pull' is one gacha roll and a 'goal' here is a target number of copies.
Title of the 2026-09-18 release note, covering interface readability and changes to the pull planner.

entries.source_text: Every route of the API is documented at /docs, and the document itself is at /api/openapi.json: 166 paths and 183 operations. Both sit outside the rate limiter, so reading the docs costs you none of your request budget.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'New'. Keep the two paths as written. The 'rate limiter' caps how many API requests a caller may make.

entries.source_text: A banner row in the pull planner printed its start date twice on the same line.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. A 'banner' is a time-limited gacha pool.

entries.source_text: In the release planner, the event list and the detail panel beside it scroll on their own instead of moving the whole page, and the list now runs to the bottom of the screen rather than stopping short.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'.

entries.source_text: Pull targets in the release planner fold away, so a banner row can be read without its full list of goals.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Improved'. 'Pull targets' is the panel heading inside a banner row and should match its translation there.

entries.source_text: Skin previews in the release planner are sized to match the rest of the site, and the note explaining where auto-translated names come from moved into the toggle's tooltip.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Improved'. A 'skin' is an operator outfit.

entries.source_text: Two trading posts were crewed one after the other against a single gold supply, so the first took the strongest squad and the second was left selling bars nobody was making. They are crewed as a pair now, judged on what the pair actually earns. On one measured account that is 42.9k LMD a day against 39.5k.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. A 'bar' is a gold bar made in an RIIC factory and sold at a trading post; LMD is the game's main currency and keeps its name.

entries.source_text: Waai Fu's Cooperative Will and Snowsant's Heavenly Reward read five times the room they sit in and so always hit their own cap. They now pay per full step of what their roommates' own skills provide. One room the game shows at 72 was being read as 77.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The two skill names are the game's own and keep their English wording. A 'room' here is an RIIC facility and the numbers are its efficiency percentage.

entries.source_text: A shift that rests an operator no longer claims the facility bonus that operator provides, so a rotation is priced against the operators actually seated in it.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. A 'shift' is one block of the base rotation the optimizer plans.

entries.source_text: 58 outfits the store sells at 15 Originium Prime were priced at 18, so a plan that picked several of them overstated its cost by 3 each. Outfit prices now match the wiki on 484 of 488.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. Originium Prime is the game's paid currency and keeps its name.

entries.source_text: Angelina's the Mellow Wish no longer renders her Elite 2 art with a flat sheet across the eyes and mouth.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'the Mellow Wish' is the outfit's own name and Elite 2 is the operator's second promotion; both keep the game's wording.

entries.source_text: The release note panel no longer cuts a line of text in half on a phone, and it shows a shadow at its edge while there is more to scroll to.
entries.description: Bullet in the second 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The 'release note panel' is the list of changes in this very dialog.

entries.source_text: Every route of the API is now documented at /docs. Three scoring bugs in the base are fixed, and unlike this morning's update these ones do move numbers: two trading posts were crewed one after the other against a single gold supply, two mirror skills read five times the room they sit in, and a shift that rested an operator still claimed his facility bonus. 58 outfits the store sells at 15 Originium Prime were priced at 18.
entries.description: Lead paragraph of the second 2026-09-19 release note, rendered as Markdown. A 'trading post' is an RIIC room and a 'mirror skill' is a base skill that copies what an operator's roommates provide; Originium Prime is the game's paid currency and keeps its name. Keep /docs as written.

entries.source_text: New: API docs, and more accurate base scoring
entries.description: Title of the second 2026-09-19 release note. 'Base' is the player's RIIC facility.

entries.source_text: The Base Optimizer and the Score tab now solve the same base, so the plan you are shown is the plan you are graded on. It seats combinations the planner used to miss.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Improved'. The Base Optimizer and the Score tab are sections of a player profile.

entries.source_text: Roster cards show an operator's alternate name in full instead of cutting off its top.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. An 'alternate name' is the second name a variant operator carries, shown above the operator's own.

entries.source_text: In the translation editor, the message key no longer breaks into single characters on a phone, and turning a page returns you to the top of the list.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The translation editor is the admin screen volunteer translators work in; a 'message key' is a string's identifier.

entries.source_text: The release note panel gets a real share of the screen on a phone rather than whatever was left over.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The 'release note panel' is the list of secondary changes in this very dialog.

entries.source_text: Promotion, potential and mastery badges on the roster are readable on the light theme again, and no longer sit on top of the module icons beside them.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Improved'. Promotion, potential, mastery and modules are in-game operator upgrade systems.

entries.source_text: The language picker is in two places instead of three, and the header now shows which language you are reading rather than a globe.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Improved'. The header shows the language's own code, such as EN or RU.

entries.source_text: In the Account Optimizer, EXP and LMD each read the same way: what is needed, what is short, and what you hold.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Improved'. The Account Optimizer is a section of a player profile; EXP and LMD are in-game currencies and keep the game's names.

entries.source_text: A trading post is valued at its own level. A level 2 post standing next to a level 3 one made both of them count as level 2, which understated the order limit and order rarity of the better room.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. A trading post is an RIIC room; 'orders' are the deliveries it produces and keep the game's name.

entries.source_text: A trading post's crew is chosen by what the post actually earns beside the factories feeding it. A gold-starved base cannot sell bonus bars, so the squad that earns more per bar wins there, while the bonus-bar squad still wins when supply is spare.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. A 'bar' is a gold bar produced by an RIIC factory and sold at a trading post.

entries.source_text: The Control Center no longer seats an operator for a clue, HR or training bonus that a stronger operator already sitting there covers.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The Control Center is an RIIC room; clues, HR and training are the kinds of bonus its base skills give and keep the game's names.

entries.source_text: Operators below milestone listed operators you had never promoted or levelled, and priced them as though you had. One section advertised a gain of 25.2 where only 13.8 was available. Your score, its breakdown and every weight are unchanged.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'Operators below milestone' is a card inside the Score tab and should match its translation there. The two numbers are grade points and are not formatted per locale.

entries.source_text: Page titles no longer collapse into a column of single letters on a phone, on the Stages page and anywhere else a heading shares a row with a counter.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-19 release note, filed under 'Fixed'.

entries.source_text: The Base Optimizer now plans with the same economy the Score tab grades you on, so the staffing it shows is the staffing you are scored against. Trading posts are valued at their own level and crewed by what they actually earn. The Operators below milestone card lists only operators you have really invested in, so the gain it advertises is one you can reach. No score, breakdown or weight has moved.
entries.description: Lead paragraph of the 2026-09-19 release note, rendered as Markdown. The Base Optimizer and the Score tab are sections of a player profile; 'Operators below milestone' is a card inside the Score tab and should match its translation there; a 'trading post' is an RIIC room and keeps the game's name.

entries.source_text: Fixed: Base planning and upgrade advice
entries.description: Title of the 2026-09-19 release note. 'Base' is the player's RIIC facility; 'upgrade advice' is the panel that ranks what to invest in next.
Label of the 2026-09-20 release note's call to action, which opens the player leaderboard.

entries.source_text: Rank the leaderboard by any item you hold. The Rank by picker searches everything anyone is holding and shows each item's icon and how many players hold it; the page keeps its shape whichever ranking you choose.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'New'. 'Rank by' is the picker's own label and should match its translation there.

entries.source_text: Tapping your nickname in the account menu left the menu sitting open over the page. It closes now, and the entry can be reached with the arrow keys.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The 'account menu' is the popup under the avatar in the site header.

entries.source_text: A row in your tier lists squeezed its own title down to a single letter on a phone and spilled its badge across the actions button. The row wraps below that width now.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'Your tier lists' is the page listing the tier lists a player made.

entries.source_text: An item ranking is a link you can share, and a player you search for keeps their true rank rather than being renumbered inside your search.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'New'.

entries.source_text: Optimizing a single base room no longer re-crews the rooms outside it or changes a factory's recipe behind your back. Rooms outside the scope are held as they are and scored that way.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Improved'. A 'factory' is an RIIC room and its 'recipe' is what it is set to produce.

entries.source_text: Reclamation Algorithm is named as such across the site, rather than Sandbox. Where a label has to be short it reads RA.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Improved'. Reclamation Algorithm is a game mode and keeps the game's name; RA is its usual abbreviation.

entries.source_text: A rotation's shifts were priced against the operators you have seated now rather than the ones the shift recommends, so any skill that depends on who else is deployed read as inactive in every shift while the stationed view counted it.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. A 'shift' is one block of the base rotation; 'stationed' is the single best staffing shown beside the rotation.

entries.source_text: On a gold-starved base Proviso takes the lower-level trading post, where her bonus on small orders pays on every order the post draws.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. Proviso is an operator, a trading post is an RIIC room and an 'order' is what it produces; all keep the game's names.

entries.source_text: An operator reserved for the Office or the Reception Room was held out of every rotation and then never actually seated there.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The Office and the Reception Room are RIIC rooms and keep the game's names.

entries.source_text: A spare Control Center seat now goes to a base-wide morale bonus first, HR or training speed next, and clue speed last whatever its size. Clue speed was counted at triple weight and beat everything.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. The Control Center is an RIIC room; morale, HR, training and clues are the kinds of bonus its base skills give and keep the game's names.

entries.source_text: Teams built around a capacity bonus were cut before they were ever compared, because the shortlist ranked on speed alone and a capacity skill scores nothing there.
entries.description: Bullet in the 2026-09-20 release note, filed under 'Fixed'. 'Capacity' is an RIIC base-skill effect that raises how much a room can hold.

entries.source_text: The leaderboard ranks by any item in your inventory, not just by score: pick LMD, Orundum, a certificate or anything else you hold, and the table, your own standing and the cards beside them all follow it. Five more base scoring bugs are fixed, and like yesterday's these do move numbers. Reclamation Algorithm is called by its name across the site instead of Sandbox.
entries.description: Lead paragraph of the 2026-09-20 release note, rendered as Markdown. LMD and Orundum are in-game currencies and Reclamation Algorithm is a game mode; all keep the game's names. 'Base' is the player's RIIC facility.

entries.source_text: New: Rank the leaderboard by anything you hold
entries.description: Title of the 2026-09-20 release note. The leaderboard could previously only be ranked by the site's own score.
Inline label in front of a release-note bullet describing a repaired bug. A past participle.
Inline label in front of a release-note bullet describing something made better. A past participle.
Inline label in front of a release-note bullet describing something newly added. An adjective.

entries.source_text: Every commit pushed to myrtle.moe, pulled live from GitHub and grouped by day.
entries.description: Caption under the changelog heading. 'myrtle.moe' is this site's name and 'GitHub' a product name; both stay as-is.

entries.source_text: Nothing landed in this window yet. Try a wider range above to see recent work.
entries.description: Empty state body under 'No commits in …'.
Empty state heading when the active window holds no commits, e.g. 'No commits in this week'. {range} is a lower-case range name. No full stop in the source.
How many commits landed on one day, shown next to that day's heading.
Heading of the commit group for the current day.
Heading of the commit group for the previous day.
Eyebrow label above the changelog page heading. Rendered uppercase.
Caption under the name of the git branch the commits were read from.
Caption under the commit count, naming the active time window, e.g. 'commits · this week'. {range} is a lower-case range name. Always plural.
Caption under the count of people who authored commits in the active window. The number itself is rendered above this label, not inside it.
Caption under the relative time of the last fetch from GitHub, shown when no branch is pinned.
Link at the foot of the changelog page, pointing at the site-statistics page. The arrow is part of the label.
Tab showing the raw commit feed rather than the hand-written notes. A noun.
Tab showing the hand-written release notes rather than the raw commit feed.
Heading of the changelog page. 'Shipped' means released to users. No full stop in the source.

entries.source_text: Older history is capped - see the full log on GitHub.
entries.description: Note under the commit feed when the fetch window hit its cap. 'GitHub' is a product name and stays as-is.
Time-window tab covering the last 24 hours.
The 'Today' window named mid-sentence, as in 'No commits in today' and 'commits · today'. Lower-case in English.
Narrow-screen form of the 'Today' time-window tab. Keep it to three or four characters.
Time-window tab covering the last thirty days. Title case in the source.
The 'This Month' window named mid-sentence, as in 'No commits in this month'. Lower-case in English.
Narrow-screen form of the 'This Month' time-window tab. 'd' is short for days.
Time-window tab covering the last ninety days. Title case in the source.
The '3 Months' window named mid-sentence, as in 'No commits in 3 months'. Lower-case in English.
Narrow-screen form of the '3 Months' time-window tab. 'd' is short for days.
Time-window tab covering the last seven days. Title case in the source.
The 'This Week' window named mid-sentence, as in 'No commits in this week'. Lower-case in English.
Narrow-screen form of the 'This Week' time-window tab. 'd' is short for days.
Accessible name of the bell button in the site header, which opens the latest release note.
Accessible name of the header bell button while an announcement has not been opened yet. The bracketed word tells a screen-reader user what the dot means.
Accessible name of the breadcrumb <nav> landmark. Lowercase on purpose: screen readers announce it as 'breadcrumb navigation'.
Screen-reader-only text behind the ellipsis that stands in for the breadcrumb steps collapsed out of the trail.
Accessible name of the small x on a selected-value chip in a multi-select combobox. A verb: it deselects that one value.
Accessible name of the x button in a dialog's top corner. A verb: it dismisses the dialog.
Accessible name of the checkmark drawn beside a ticked drawer menu checkbox item. A state, not a verb.
Accessible name of the x button in a drawer's top corner. A verb: it dismisses the drawer.
Accessible name of the checkmark drawn beside the chosen drawer menu radio item. A state, not a verb.

entries.source_text: You're offline. Check your connection and try again.
entries.description: Error toast body when the browser reports no network connection.

entries.source_text: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
entries.description: Error toast body when the server refused the request for being sent too often (HTTP 429).
Error toast body when the server refused the request and gave no readable reason. {status} is the HTTP status number.

entries.source_text: The server ran into a problem ({status}). Try again in a minute.
entries.description: Error toast body for an unexpected error on the server (HTTP 5xx). {status} is the number.

entries.source_text: Signed in, but the first roster sync failed ({status}). Reload the page: your account is connected, and you can sync again from your profile.
entries.description: Error toast body after a successful sign-in whose immediate roster download failed. {status} is the HTTP status number.

entries.source_text: The server took too long to respond. Try again in a moment.
entries.description: Error toast body when the request timed out waiting for the server.

entries.source_text: You're not allowed to do that ({status}). If you were signed in, your session may have expired.
entries.description: Error toast body when the server rejected the request as unauthorized or forbidden (HTTP 401 or 403). {status} is the number.

entries.source_text: The server is temporarily unavailable ({status}). Try again in a minute.
entries.description: Error toast body when the server is up but cannot serve requests right now (HTTP 503). {status} is the number.
Error toast body when the failure carried no message at all.

entries.source_text: The server couldn't be reached. It may be down or restarting; try again in a minute.
entries.description: Error toast body when the request got no answer from the server at all.

entries.source_text: The server couldn't be reached ({code}). It may be down or restarting; try again in a minute.
entries.description: Same as errorMessage.unreachable, with the low-level network code in parentheses. {code} is a technical identifier such as ECONNREFUSED and stays as-is.

entries.source_text: built on TanStack Start · COSS UI
entries.description: Credit line in the footer. Lowercase on purpose. 'TanStack Start' and 'COSS UI' are product names and stay as-is; only 'built on' is translatable.
Footer link to the site's release notes.

entries.source_text: Not affiliated with Hypergryph or Yostar. Game data and assets are property of their respective owners.
entries.description: Legal disclaimer in the footer. 'Hypergryph' and 'Yostar' are company names and stay as-is.
Footer link to the community chat. 'Discord' is a product name and stays as-is.
Footer link to the donation page. A verb.
Footer link to the privacy policy. Short by design; it sits in a single row of small links.
Accessible name of the footer <nav> landmark holding the changelog, legal and community links.
Footer link to the terms of service. Short by design; it sits in a single row of small links.

A noun naming what the language controls select. Used as the screen-reader-only group label in the footer switcher, the heading of the header's globe menu and of the mobile drawer's language group, and the title of the Language card in appearance settings.
Tooltip and accessible name of the bold button. The parenthesised part is the keyboard shortcut and stays as-is.
Tooltip and accessible name of the button that turns the selected lines into an unordered list.
Accessible name of the toolbar row holding the bold/italic/list buttons.
Tooltip and accessible name of the button that wraps the selection in backticks.
Tooltip and accessible name of the italic button. The parenthesised part is the keyboard shortcut and stays as-is.
Tooltip and accessible name of the insert-link button. The parenthesised part is the keyboard shortcut and stays as-is.
Narrow-screen hint under the editor, standing in for the desktop syntax cheatsheet. 'Markdown' is the name of the markup language and normally stays as-is.
Shown on the Preview tab while the editor is still empty.
Tooltip and accessible name of the button that turns the selected lines into an ordered list.
Tab that shows the rendered Markdown. A verb, paired with the 'Write' tab; it sits in a narrow tab so keep it short.
Tooltip and accessible name of the button that turns the selected lines into a block quote. A verb.
Tab that shows the editable textarea. A verb, paired with the 'Preview' tab; it sits in a narrow tab so keep it short.

entries.source_text: The page you are looking for does not exist, has been moved, or is temporarily unavailable.
entries.description: Body copy of the 404 page.
Primary 404 action: navigates to the site root.
Secondary 404 action: opens the command palette.
Heading of the 404 page. A Terra-flavoured 'page not found'; a literal translation is fine if the setting has no equivalent.
Accessible name of the pager <nav> landmark. Lowercase on purpose: screen readers announce it as 'pagination navigation'.
Screen-reader-only text behind the ellipsis that stands in for skipped page numbers.
Visible label beside the forward arrow. Hidden below the sm breakpoint, so keep it short.
Accessible name of the next-page control, which shows only an arrow on small screens.
Visible label beside the back arrow. Hidden below the sm breakpoint, so keep it short.
Accessible name of the previous-page control, which shows only an arrow on small screens.
Suffix on an operator row for an operator that exists only on the Chinese server so far. 'CN' is the server's short name and stays as-is.
Shown when the operator index loaded but nothing in it matches. {query} is the text the visitor typed, quoted.
Shown when nothing in any group matches the query.
Group heading above matching operators (playable characters).

entries.source_text: Failed to load operators. Try reopening the palette.
entries.description: Shown in place of the operator list when its request failed.
Group heading above matching site pages.
Placeholder in the command palette's search field. Ends in a single ellipsis character.
Attribution in the palette footer. 'COSS UI' is a product name and stays as-is.
Footer hint, read after the up and down arrow key caps: 'up down to navigate'.
Footer hint, read after the enter key cap: 'enter to select'.
Group heading above matching tools (calculators, planners).
Accessible name of the x button in a sheet's top corner. A verb: it dismisses the sheet.
Screen-reader-only description of that same sheet. Never visible.
Screen-reader-only title of the sheet the sidebar becomes on small screens. Never visible.
Accessible name and tooltip of the control that collapses or expands the sidebar. A verb: one control does both directions.
Accessible name of the spinning busy indicator, announced while something is still being fetched. No trailing ellipsis.
Heading of the bucket holding limited-time events and their reruns.
Heading of the bucket holding the game's always-available modes (Annihilation, Integrated Strategies and so on).
Heading of the bucket holding mainline campaign operations.
Part of a stage chip's hover text, in place of a spawn count, when the enemy only appears if something summons it or a condition is met.
Part of a stage chip's hover text: how many of this enemy the operation sends. Joined to the stage name with ' · '.

entries.source_text: This enemy isn't listed in any of the currently extracted level files. Coverage grows as more content is processed.
entries.description: Empty-state paragraph in the Appears In tab, explaining the gap is this site's coverage rather than the game's.
Empty-state heading in the Appears In tab when no level file mentions this enemy.

entries.source_text: Found in {locations} {locationCount, plural, one {location} other {locations}} across {zones} {zoneCount, plural, one {zone} other {zones}}.
entries.description: Sentence above the appearance list, e.g. 'Found in 12 locations across 4 zones.'. {locations} and {zones} are the two bold counts and may move anywhere the sentence needs them; {locationCount} and {zoneCount} are the same numbers again, used only to pick the plural form.
Sub-heading inside an event, over its EX operations. 'EX' is the game's own prefix for the harder event stages; keep it.
Sub-heading inside an event, over its normal operations (as opposed to its EX ones).
Badge on a zone row: the Annihilation game mode. An in-game mode name; keep the game's own name for it.
Badge on a zone row: a Vignette / branchline event. Short badge, so keep it brief.
Badge on a zone row: a limited-time event.
Badge on a zone row: a tutorial zone.
Badge on a zone row: the Integrated Strategies game mode, abbreviated. An in-game mode name; keep the game's own abbreviation.
Badge on a zone row: part of the mainline campaign. Short badge, so keep it brief.
Badge on a zone row: a Side Story event. The game's own category name.
Badge on a zone row: a special zone outside the usual categories.
Badge on a zone row: the Stationary Security Service game mode, abbreviated. An in-game mode name; keep the game's own abbreviation.
Badge on a zone row: a weekly resource-farming zone.
Attack range of an enemy: it strikes adjacent tiles only.
Attack range of an enemy: it has no attack at all.
Attack range of an enemy: it strikes at a distance.
Accessible name of an enemy card in the grid. {name} is the enemy's name and {index} its in-game handbook callsign, both game data; only the punctuation around them is yours.
Stat bar label on an enemy grid card: attack. Fixed 20px column, so it must stay this short.
Stat bar label on an enemy grid card: defense. Fixed 20px column, so it must stay this short.
Stat bar label on an enemy grid card: hit points. Fixed 20px column, so it must stay this short.
Alt text of an enemy's portrait image on a grid card. {name} is the enemy's name from the game data.
Accessible name of an enemy row in the list view. {name} is the enemy's name and {index} its in-game handbook callsign, both game data; only the punctuation around them is yours.
Alt text of an enemy's portrait image on a list row. {name} is the enemy's name from the game data.
Shown in the Chibi tab when the chibi index request fails. 'Chibi' is the game's small animated sprite.

entries.source_text: No chibi available for this enemy.
entries.description: Shown in the Chibi tab when the game data ships no animated sprite for this enemy.
Label before the damage-type filter chips. Short uppercase label on the chip rail.
Label before the race filter chips; the race names themselves are game data.
Label before the Melee / Ranged / None filter chips. Short uppercase label on the chip rail.
Label before the Normal / Elite / Boss filter chips. Short uppercase label on the chip rail.
Damage type an enemy deals: it heals rather than harms.
Damage type an enemy deals: magic damage, mitigated by RES. 'Arts' is the game's own name for magic; keep the game's term.
Damage type an enemy deals: none - it does not attack.
Damage type an enemy deals: ordinary physical damage, mitigated by DEF.
Accessible name of the breadcrumb <nav> landmark above the enemy's name.
First breadcrumb crumb, naming the section the enemy handbook lives in.
Breadcrumb link back to the enemy list. The last crumb is the enemy's own name, which is game data.
Link out of the enemy-not-found page, back to the enemy list.

entries.source_text: No enemy with id {id} exists in the handbook.
entries.description: Shown when the URL names an enemy id the backend has no enemy for. {id} is that id, rendered in a monospace box, and may move wherever the sentence needs it. 'Handbook' is the game's own enemy reference screen.
Heading shown when the URL names an enemy id the backend has no enemy for.
Tab label: which stages the enemy shows up in.
Tab label: the enemy's animated sprite. 'Chibi' is the game community's word for it.
Tab label: the enemy's description, traits and tags.
Tab label: the enemy's skills and their cooldowns.
Tab label: the enemy's stat blocks and status immunities.
Threat tier: a boss enemy. Shown as a short uppercase badge, so keep it brief.
Threat tier: a tougher, named variant. Shown as a short uppercase badge, so keep it brief.
Threat tier: an ordinary enemy. Also the filter chip for that tier.

entries.source_text: View all {count} enemies catalogued in Arknights, sorted by Hypergryph's internal sort index by default.
entries.description: Paragraph under the enemy-list heading. {count} is the bold number of enemies and may move wherever the sentence needs it. 'Arknights' and 'Hypergryph' are the game and its developer; keep both names.
Accessible name of the breadcrumb <nav> landmark at the top of the enemy list.
First breadcrumb crumb, naming the section the enemy list lives in.
Last breadcrumb crumb: this page.
Inline link after the result count that drops every active filter, counting how many are on.
List-view column header: what damage type the enemy deals.
List-view column header: hit points. Abbreviated to fit a narrow, right-aligned column.
List-view column header: the enemy's name and callsign.
List-view column header: the Normal / Elite / Boss tier.

entries.source_text: Adjust the chip rail or your search above, or clear everything and start fresh.
entries.description: Empty-state paragraph. 'Chip rail' is the row of filter chips above the results.
Empty-state button that drops every active filter.
Empty-state heading when the filters and search match no enemy.
Label on the export button, hidden on phone widths where only the icon shows.
Accessible name of the export button, and its tooltip.
Headline of the export dialog, naming what is being exported.
Hint beside the pager, hidden on phone widths, telling the reader a card opens the enemy's page.
Page-size option: put every result on one page.
Accessible name of the page-size select.
Uppercase prefix inside the page-size select, before the number of rows. Very tight space.
Accessible name of the <main> landmark holding the filters, the result grid and the pager.
Accessible name of the enemy search box.

entries.source_text: Search by name, callsign, or race…
entries.description: Placeholder in the enemy search box. 'Callsign' is the enemy's handbook index, e.g. 'B1'. Ends with a single ellipsis character.
Result count above the pager, e.g. 'Showing 1-48 of 412 enemies'. All three numbers are bold and may move wherever the sentence needs them. No closing full stop: a link may follow after a middle dot.
Accessible name of the sort select.
Hover title of the sort-direction button when the current order is ascending.
Hover title of the sort-direction button when the current order is descending.
Uppercase prefix inside the sort select, before the chosen sort option. Very tight space.
Accessible name of the button that flips between ascending and descending.
Page heading of the enemy list.
Accessible name of the grid/list toggle button group.
Grid view button: its tooltip and its hover title. Shows enemies as portrait cards.
List view button: its tooltip and its hover title. Shows enemies as compact rows.
Button in the location filter's footer that unselects every location.
Accessible name of that same checkbox when everything under it is already selected.
Empty state inside the location filter when the search matches no event, mode or stage.
Accessible name of the x on a selected-location chip. {name} is the event or stage name, which is game data.
Accessible name of the location filter's search box.
Accessible name of the small x button that empties the location filter's search box.
Placeholder in the location filter's search box. Ends with a single ellipsis character.
Accessible name of a checkbox that selects every stage under a category or event. {name} is the category or event name, which is game data.
Footer of the location filter, counting how many locations are picked.
Label on the button that opens the location filter, i.e. which stages an enemy shows up in.
Accessible name of the 'Appears In' filter button, spelling out what the short label means.
Kicker over the enemy's handbook blurb. The blurb itself is game data.
Metadata field label; its value is a game-data identifier and is never translated.
Metadata field label: whether the game shows this enemy in its own handbook screen.
Value of the In Handbook field when the game hides this enemy from its handbook.
Metadata field label; its value is a race name from the game data.
Metadata field label: the number the game orders the handbook by.
Value of the In Handbook field when the game lists this enemy in its handbook.
Kicker over the grid of raw backend fields for this enemy.
Kicker over the enemy's tag pills. The tags themselves are game data.
Kicker over the enemy's ability list. The ability text itself is game data.
Accessible name (SVG <title>) of the stand-in drawing shown when an enemy has no portrait. Never seen, only announced.
Skill card field label: seconds between uses.

entries.source_text: No skills active in this form.
entries.description: Shown under one stat block's heading when that form has no skills, and the handbook names the forms.

entries.source_text: No skills active in this level.
entries.description: Shown under one stat block's heading when that level has no skills, and the handbook names none of them.

entries.source_text: Skill kit is identical across all {phases} {count, plural, one {form} other {forms}}.
entries.description: Shown above the skill list when every stat block carries the same skills and the handbook names each one as a form. {phases} is the bold count and may move; {count} is the same number again, used only to pick the plural form. 'Kit' is the set of skills an enemy has.

entries.source_text: Skill kit is identical across all {phases} {count, plural, one {level} other {levels}}.
entries.description: The same line when the handbook names none of the stat blocks, so they are levels rather than forms. {phases} is the bold count and may move; {count} is the same number again, used only to pick the plural form.
Skill card field label: the cooldown the skill starts the battle on. 'CD' abbreviates cooldown; very tight space.

entries.source_text: No skill data available for this enemy.
entries.description: Shown in the Skills tab when no stat block carries any skill.
Skill card field label: skill points needed to fire. 'SP' is the game's own abbreviation.
Sort option: by attack. Abbreviated to fit a compact select.
Sort option: by defense. Abbreviated to fit a compact select.
Sort option: by hit points. Abbreviated to fit a compact select.
Sort option: by the enemy's in-game handbook index (its callsign, e.g. 'B1'). Short label in a compact select.
Sort option: by threat tier (Normal, then Elite, then Boss). Short label in a compact select.
Sort option: alphabetically by enemy name. Short label in a compact select.
Sort option: by magic resistance. Abbreviated to fit a compact select.
Sort option: by mass level, which decides how far the enemy can be shoved. Short label in a compact select.
Kicker over the stat blocks when the enemy has only one.

entries.source_text: Combat · {count, plural, one {# form} other {# forms}}
entries.description: Kicker over the stat blocks when the handbook names each of them, so they read as the enemy's transformation forms.

entries.source_text: Combat · {count, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}}
entries.description: Kicker over the stat blocks when the handbook names none of them, so they read as the game data's numbered levels.

entries.source_text: This enemy transforms across {forms} forms in-fight, but Hypergryph's data ships {count, plural, one {a single stat block} other {# stat blocks}}. Subsequent forms modify behavior through skill triggers rather than swapping the base HP/ATK/DEF - see {traits} for the form descriptions.
entries.description: Note explaining why an enemy with several narrative forms has fewer stat blocks. {forms} is the bold form count and {traits} the bold pointer labelled by stats.forms.note.traits; both may move wherever the sentence needs them. 'Hypergryph' is the game's developer; keep the name.
The bold pointer inside that note, naming this page's Overview tab and its Traits section. Must match those two labels.
Kicker over the table of status effects the enemy shrugs off.
Accessible name of a tick in the immunity table. {status} is a status effect and {phase} the stat block's heading.
Accessible name of a cross in the immunity table. {status} is a status effect and {phase} the stat block's heading.
Status effect in the immunity table. The game's own term for it.
Status effect in the immunity table: lifted off the ground. The game's own term for it.
Status effect in the immunity table: skills blocked. The game's own term for it.
Status effect in the immunity table. The game's own term for it.
First column header of the immunity table, over the status-effect names.
Status effect in the immunity table. The game's own term for it.
Only value column header of the immunity table, used when the enemy has a single stat block so there is no form to name.

entries.source_text: No stats available for this enemy.
entries.description: Shown in the Stats tab when the game data ships no stat block at all.
Heading of one stat block when the enemy has several and the handbook names none of them. {level} counts from 0, as the game data does.
Heading of the only stat block, when the enemy has just one. Sits in a narrow pill.
Stat row label: attack speed. The game community's abbreviation; keep it short.
Stat row label: attack. Abbreviated to fit a narrow two-column list.
Stat row label: seconds between attacks before attack-speed scaling.
Stat row label: defense. Abbreviated to fit a narrow two-column list.
Stat row label: maximum hit points.
Stat row label: tiles travelled per second.
Stat row label: magic resistance as a percentage. Abbreviated to fit a narrow two-column list.
Stat row label: mass level, which decides how far the enemy can be shoved.
Banner bucket: a limited-time headhunting pool. Its pity counter does not carry over once the banner closes.
Banner bucket: a crossover banner run with another franchise. Short for collaboration; the space is tight.
Banner bucket: the ordinary rotating headhunting pool.
Banner bucket: the pool of older operators. 'Kernel' is the game's own name for it.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: one operator boosted and guaranteed within a pull count.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: the pool of older operators. 'Kernel' is the game's own name for it.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: a Kernel pool with a boosted rate on one operator. Keep the middle dot.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: a Kernel pool with two operators boosted. Keep the middle dot.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: two operators boosted at once.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: the anniversary Kernel pool. Keep the middle dot.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: a limited-time pool.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: a crossover banner. 'Joint operation' is the game's own wording for it.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: the ordinary rotating pool.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: one newly released operator at a boosted rate. 'Rate-up' is the community term for a boosted drop chance.
Readable name for a banner's rule type: anything that fits none of the other buckets.
Banner status pill: the banner is running right now.
Banner status pill: the banner has closed.
Banner status pill: the banner has been announced but has not opened yet.
Last breadcrumb crumb: this page.
First breadcrumb crumb, naming the section this page lives in. 'Gacha' is the game's random-draw system and stays as-is.
Accessible name of the breadcrumb trail above the community gacha heading.
How far an observed rate sits from its baseline, scaled to that baseline: 'above by 147%', 'below by 39%'. Lowercase; it sits in a row of small stats.
An observed drop rate that matches its baseline within one percent. Lowercase; it sits in a row of small stats.
Used instead of a percentage once the observed rate is more than ten times the baseline, e.g. '12.4× baseline'. The × is a multiplication sign.
An observed rate as a share of the expected one, e.g. '61% of expected' for a rate well under, '247% of expected' for one well over.
Bold lead-in of the error banner on the community gacha page; the server's own message follows it on the same line.
Stand-in for the server's error message when the failed request carried none.

entries.source_text: Aggregated across {doctors} who opted into anonymous sharing. Rates are observational, not official.
entries.description: Sentence under the community gacha heading. {doctors} is the bold count of contributing players, labelled by community.header.blurbUsers, and may move wherever the sentence needs it.
The bold count in the sentence under the community gacha heading. 'Player' is the site's term; the game itself says 'Doctor'.
Chip shown when the figures came from the server's cache rather than a fresh computation. Rendered in uppercase by the style.
Heading of the community gacha page. {emphasis} is the accent-coloured word labelled by community.header.titleEmphasis and may sit anywhere the sentence needs it. Keep the full stop.
The accent-coloured word substituted into community.header.title as {emphasis}. 'Pulling' is the community term for spending on headhunting.
Chip saying how long ago the figures were recomputed, e.g. 'updated 5m ago'. Lowercase, in a very narrow chip.
Under the average pulls per 6-star: the same average for 5-stars. Lowercase; keep the middle dot.
Label over the average number of pulls between 6-star operators. Rendered uppercase; 'Avg' is abbreviated because the tile is narrow.
Label over the share of pulls that produced a 5-star operator, across the whole community corpus. Rendered uppercase; keep the star and the middle dot.
Under the 5-star rate: how many 5-stars the community pulled in total.
Label over the share of pulls that produced a 6-star operator, across the whole community corpus. Rendered uppercase; keep the star and the middle dot.
Under the 6-star rate: how many 6-stars came out of how many pulls.
Label over the community's total pull count. Rendered uppercase.
Under the total pull count: how many players shared their records. 'Player' is the site's term; the game itself says 'Doctor'.
Column heading for the operator's name. Rendered uppercase.
Column heading for how many times the community pulled that operator. Rendered uppercase in a narrow column.
Column heading for that operator's percentage of all pulls of its rarity. Rendered uppercase in a narrow column.

entries.source_text: No data for this rarity yet.
entries.description: Empty state when nobody has shared a pull of the selected rarity.
Small uppercase label above the most-pulled operators panel. Keep the middle dot.
Heading of the panel ranking the operators the community pulled most often.
Tooltip on the tick marking the advertised rate on a rarity bar. {value} is already a formatted percentage.
Tooltip on the tick marking the viewer's own rate on a rarity bar. {value} is already a formatted percentage.
Label on the chip comparing the community's observed rate against the advertised one. Rendered uppercase in a tight row.
Label on the chip comparing the viewer's own rate against the community's. Rendered uppercase in a tight row.
Label on the chip comparing the viewer's own rate against the advertised one. Rendered uppercase in a tight row.
The advertised 5-star odds: an 8% chance per pull, with one guaranteed in the first ten pulls. Keep the middle dot.
The advertised 4-star odds: half of all pulls.
The advertised 6-star odds: a 2% chance per pull, rising by two points per pull once fifty pulls have passed without one. Keep the middle dot.
The advertised 3-star odds: two pulls in five.
Small uppercase label above the rarity-distribution panel, used while the pull total is still loading.
Small uppercase label above the rarity-distribution panel once the total is known. Keep the middle dot.
Legend entry for the tick showing the advertised rate. 'Pity' is the game's rising-chance mechanic; the advertised rate is adjusted for it.

entries.source_text: expected rates fold 6★ soft pity into the advertised 2/8/50/40% base - long-run 6★ is ~2.89%, and lower rarities dip slightly because a pity 6★ takes their slot
entries.description: Legend footnote explaining how the expected rates were derived. 'Soft pity' is the game's rising 6-star chance after fifty pulls.

entries.source_text: comparisons scale to baseline (e.g. 4% vs 2.89% expected = 138% of expected, not "+1.1%")
entries.description: Legend footnote explaining that the comparison chips express a ratio of the baseline rather than a point difference.
Legend entry for the tick showing the viewer's own rate. Rendered uppercase.
How many pulls landed on this rarity, under its bar.
Heading of the panel breaking all pulls down by rarity.
Pill marking the viewer's own column in the rarity panel. Lowercase, rendered uppercase by the style; keep the middle dot.
How long ago the community figures were recomputed, in days. Abbreviated to a single letter - the chip it sits in is very narrow.
How long ago the community figures were recomputed, in hours. Abbreviated to a single letter - the chip it sits in is very narrow.
How long ago the community figures were recomputed, in minutes. Abbreviated to a single letter - the chip it sits in is very narrow.
How long ago the community figures were recomputed, for anything under a minute. Lowercase; it follows the word 'updated'.
Unit after the pull count on a banner card. Rendered uppercase.
Tooltip on a banner card's player count. 'Player' is the site's term; the game itself says 'Doctor'.
A banner's run window, e.g. 'Mar 3, 2025 → Mar 17, 2025'. Keep the arrow.
Empty state when the chosen filter leaves no banners in the list.
Label over the row of 6-star operators a banner boosts. Rendered uppercase.
Label of the segmented control choosing which banners are listed. Rendered uppercase.
Banner filter: only banners running right now. Fits a narrow segmented button.
Banner filter: every banner in the window. Fits a narrow segmented button.
A banner's guarantee, e.g. 'Guaranteed 5★ within 10 pulls'. {name} is the guarantee's own name from the game data where it has one.
Stand-in name for a banner's guarantee when the game data leaves it blank.
Small uppercase label above the panel listing recent, running and announced banners.
Names the metric a card was ranked by, inside the rank tooltip: 'Ranked #3 by contributing doctors'. 'Player' is the site's term; the game itself says 'Doctor'.
Names the metric a card was ranked by, inside the rank tooltip: 'Ranked #3 by community pulls'.
Tooltip on the '+3' chip that stands in for featured operators the card has no room to show.
Shown on a banner card when nobody who shares their records has pulled on it. Rendered uppercase.
Compact player count on a banner card, e.g. '1.2k ppl'. 'ppl' abbreviates people; the space is a non-breaking one and the card is narrow.
Tooltip on a banner card's rank badge while a metric sort is active.
Button that expands the banner list to every match. Rendered uppercase.
Button that collapses the banner list back to the first page. Rendered uppercase.
Label of the segmented control choosing how the banner cards are ordered. Rendered uppercase.
Banner sort: most contributing players first. Fits a narrow segmented button.
Banner sort: most community pulls first. Fits a narrow segmented button.
Banner sort: running first, then announced, then most recently ended. Fits a narrow segmented button.
Banner-runs heading when at least one banner is running. {count} is the accent-coloured number of running banners and may sit anywhere the sentence needs it.
Banner-runs heading used when no banner is running at the moment.
Tooltip on a banner's run bar under the chart: the banner's name, then its bucket. The name comes from the game data.
Heading over the day-by-day activity chart, saying how long the window is. Rendered uppercase; keep the middle dot.
Heading over the day-of-week chart. Rendered uppercase.
Heading over the hour-of-day chart. The hours are in UTC rather than the viewer's zone. Rendered uppercase; keep the middle dot.
Last line of the chart's hover card when more banners were running that day than the card can list.
Unit after the pull count in the chart's hover card, e.g. '1,204 pulls'. Rendered uppercase.
Small uppercase label above the charts showing when the community pulls.
Chart legend entry for the line showing all pulls, whatever the banner. Rendered uppercase.
Heading of the panel charting pull activity over time.
Column heading for the banner a pull was made on. Rendered uppercase.
Column heading for when a pull was made. Rendered uppercase.
Column heading for the operator a pull produced. Rendered uppercase.

entries.source_text: No pulls recorded for this banner type.
entries.description: Empty state when the selected banner bucket holds none of the player's pulls.

entries.source_text: No {rarities} pulls in {tab}. Other rarities are hidden by the filter.
entries.description: Empty state when the rarity filter leaves the selected banner bucket with nothing. {rarities} is a list of star counts like '6★ 5★'; {tab} is the bucket's name.

entries.source_text: Select at least one rarity to display pulls.
entries.description: Empty state when every rarity chip has been switched off, so nothing can be listed.
Small uppercase label above the full list of the player's pulls.
Pager button for the next page. The button is tiny.
Pager button for the previous page. Abbreviated; the button is tiny.
Pager summary under the table, e.g. '51-100 of 2,431 pulls'.
Describes the rarity filter when every chip is switched off. Read out to screen readers.
Describes the rarity filter when exactly one chip is on, e.g. '6★ only'. Read out to screen readers.
Accessible name of one rarity filter chip, naming the rarity and how many of the player's pulls it holds.
Label before the row of rarity filter chips. Rendered uppercase.
Button inside the empty state that switches every rarity chip back on.
Screen-reader-only summary when no rarity is filtered out.
Screen-reader-only summary of the active filter. {rarities} describes the rarity chips; {tab} is the banner bucket's name.

entries.source_text: Scoring is subject to change and in the very early stages of development. Score is based off of potential completion, NOT how "meta" your account is.
entries.description: Notice above the score cards. 'Meta' is community slang for the strongest current picks, hence the quotation marks; the capitalised NOT is emphasis and should stay emphatic.
Small uppercase tag marking the scoring feature as unfinished.
Tooltip on one segment of the composition bar. {label} is a section name, {earned} the points earned and {share} the points available; 'pts' is short for points.
Card title over the bar showing how much each section contributes to the overall grade.

entries.description: Empty-state body on the Score tab. 'Doctor' is what Arknights calls the player; keep the apostrophes.
Empty-state title on the Score tab when this account has never been graded.
Unit after a worldwide rank number, e.g. '#1,204 global'. Also used in the score-history tooltip.

entries.source_text: History builds one point per leaderboard snapshot - check back after the next one.
entries.description: Shown in place of the chart when there are fewer than two snapshots to plot.
Placeholder while the score snapshots are being fetched. Keep the single-character ellipsis.
Card title over the chart of total score over time.

entries.source_text: {delta} pts over {count, plural, one {# point} other {# points}}
entries.description: Chip beside the chart title summarising the change across the series; an up or down arrow precedes it. 'pts' is short for points of score, while {count} counts plotted data points.

entries.source_text: Component breakdown appears after the next score refresh.
entries.description: Shown in the Base panel for an account whose stored score predates the component split.

entries.source_text: What your rooms can achieve as built, against the same rooms at max level.
entries.description: Blurb under the Upgrades component.
Name of the Base component covering how far the rooms themselves are built up.

entries.source_text: Plan restaffing and see the full room-by-room comparison in the Optimizer tab.
entries.description: Footer of the Base panel pointing at the profile's Optimizer tab, whose name is translated on the tab strip.
Heading over the Base subscore's two components.

entries.source_text: You've earned every medal that's currently reachable. Nice work.

Pill on an event medal whose window closes today. Lowercase on purpose.

Heading of the group of medals that can only be earned while their event runs.

Heading of the group of medals that need an operator the account cannot currently obtain.
Count badge on a medal list heading. {n} is how many medals in that group the account is missing.

Button that reveals a medal group that starts collapsed. {n} is how many medals it holds.

entries.description: Blurb under the 'No longer obtainable' heading. 'Towers' are the in-game Stultifera Navis-style tower events.
